search_log: Searched “All the Colors of the Dark Chris Whitaker excerpt first chapter,” publisher excerpts, and PRH pages; found sustained third-person opening prose from Penguin Random House and a duplicate authorized Bookreporter excerpt.
Searched the title with “third person,” “point of view,” “narrator,” and “multiple points of view”; found BookRags' explicit whole-book third-person analysis.

Searched exact text from the apparent first-person quotations (“The shrink they make me see,” “We look at others with fucking trivial problems,” “To ask forgiveness for acts I know in my heart,” and “sometimes things survive”); no indexed contextual matches were found.

Checked Google Books, Hachette UK, SuperSummary, reader-guide, epistolary, frame-narrative, and interior-excerpt leads; Google Books and publisher samples did not expose a different interior narrative person, and no credible source described alternating first-person sections.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, shifting limited focalization chiefly between Patch and Saint. Multiple Goodreads event passages externally name these characters while reporting their knowledge, perceptions, and private responses; the authorized opening independently uses the same pattern, and the whole-book study guide explicitly identifies third person throughout. The isolated I/we passages in q08775, q08776, q08783, and q08791 are therefore local speech or direct thought, with likely lost quotation boundaries or upstream bucket issues, rather than sustained first-person sections. No credible evidence supports second person or alternating person. The only residual uncertainty is the exact local attribution of those clipped first-person fragments, which does not affect the book-level label.
